blueprint_concepts: Tangent and normal to a circle
Tangent to the parabola: point, slope and parametric forms

concept_use.Tangent and normal to a circle: Tangency of the parabola's tangent to C: the perpendicular distance from the centre S equals the radius sqrt 5.
concept_use.Tangent to the parabola: point, slope an: Parametric tangent t y = x + t^2 at (t^2, 2t) of the parabola gives every common tangent and its point of contact.

english: Let $S$ be the focus of the parabola $y^{2}=4x$ and let $C$ be the circle $(x-1)^{2}+y^{2}=5$. The common tangents of the parabola and $C$ touch the parabola at the points $P$ and $Q$. Then the area of the triangle $SPQ$ is
hindi: माना कि $S$ परवलय $y^{2}=4x$ की नाभि है तथा $C$ वृत्त $(x-1)^{2}+y^{2}=5$ है। परवलय तथा $C$ की उभयनिष्ठ स्पर्श रेखाएँ परवलय को बिन्दुओं $P$ तथा $Q$ पर स्पर्श करती हैं। तब त्रिभुज $SPQ$ का क्षेत्रफल है
solution: Tangent to the parabola at $(t^{2},2t)$: $ty=x+t^{2}$. Its distance from $S(1,0)$ is $\dfrac{1+t^{2}}{\sqrt{1+t^{2}}}=\sqrt{1+t^{2}}$
Every tangent of the parabola has this form, so $P=(4,4)$, $Q=(4,-4)$
solution_full: The circle $C$ has centre $(1,0)$, which is the focus $S$ of $y^{2}=4x$, and radius $\sqrt{5}$.
Every tangent of the parabola is the tangent at some point $(t^{2},2t)$: $ty=x+t^{2}$, i.e. $x-ty+t^{2}=0$.
The line is tangent to $C$ when this distance equals the radius: $\sqrt{1+t^{2}}=\sqrt{5}$, so $t^{2}=4$, $t=\pm2$.
So there are exactly two common tangents, $2y=x+4$ and $-2y=x+4$, touching the parabola at $P=(4,4)$ and $Q=(4,-4)$.
Triangle $SPQ$: base $PQ=8$ on the line $x=4$, and the distance of $S(1,0)$ from this line is $3$.
originality_note: New: a circle centred at the focus, where the distance from the focus to the tangent at t is sqrt(1 + t^2), so the common-tangent condition collapses to t^2 = 4 (way 4, a hidden clean invariant). Closest known: common tangents of a parabola and a circle in slope form (for example y^2 = 8x and x^2 + y^2 = 2). Different because: the circle is centred at the focus, the tangency condition reduces to a focal-distance condition, and the area asked uses the parabola contact points with the focus.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, curve and parameter is introduced, the conditions are complete, there is one reading, the answer is unique and equals the Answer Plan, the options have one form and the Hindi mirrors the English. Checked that no other line (vertical or the axis) is a common tangent, so exactly two tangents and two contact points. Answer 12 at (A) as planned. No change.
key_step: Distance from the focus to the tangent at t is sqrt(1 + t^2); equate to sqrt 5 to get t = +-2.
justification: Parametric tangent plus the distance condition, then a triangle area: a routine chain with a pleasant simplification, no new idea. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q2 (L2) on parabola tangents.
